claims.statement: For the original fixed selector F(T,p), the primary aggregate is exactly Q_p-Q_(p-1), where Q_j=sum over v in F of i_j(H_v)-i_j(R_v). For each v, H_v splits into rooted tree components and its marked polynomial is the product difference prod_i I(C_i)-prod_i I(C_i-w_i), with the positive component recurrence stated in REPORT.md. This reduces the route to a fixed marked-rank comparison but does not prove its sign.
claims.scope: Exact identities for every finite ordinary tree and eligible (T,p), with original distinct leaf tags and fixed F(T,p); bounded exact computations cover all labeled trees through order 8 (no eligible rows) and the pinned T_m family for m<=8 only.
claims.reason: The recurrence and rank-difference identities are exact, and all 13 eligible bounded T_m rows replay with negative S. The order-1-through-8 labeled census has no eligible rows. No argument transports the first descent of I(T) to Q_p<=Q_(p-1) in general, and no eligible full-sum refutation was found; leave the primary assertion open.

limitations: No proof of the required aggregate marked-rank comparison for arbitrary ordinary trees was established.
The all-labeled-tree census ends at order 8 and contains no eligible rows; it gives no sign information on eligible inputs.
The T_m calculation covers only m=1 through 8 and is bounded computation, not a family theorem.
No public literature result was imported or used to close the transport gap.
